name: Ivermectin
executiveSummary: Macrocyclic lactone anthelmintic/ectoparasiticide. Strongyloidiasis/onchocerciasis: **200 µg/kg PO once** (sometimes repeat). Scabies (protocols): **200 µg/kg** ± day 7–14. 3 mg tablets — weight-based.
indications:
## Indications

- Strongyloidiasis; onchocerciasis.
- Scabies/pediculosis in institutional regimens (off-label in some countries).

## Precautions

- Avoid in pregnancy; caution in lactation.
- Neurologic risk with *Loa loa* co-infection (Africa) — screen first.
- Not a COVID-19 treatment outside trials.

> Many labels: empty stomach with water; some with food — follow local SmPC.

adulto.dose: **200 µg/kg PO** rounded to 3 mg multiples. Approx: 15–24 kg → 3 mg; 25–35 → 6 mg; 36–50 → 9 mg; 51–65 → 12 mg; 66–79 → 15 mg; ≥80 kg → **200 µg/kg**. Scabies: often **repeat day 7 or 14**.
adulto.administration: PO single dose. Onchocerciasis: WHO community regimens differ.
adulto.notes: Weigh the patient; do not guess.

pediatrico.presentation: 3 mg tabs (crush if allowed by label).
pediatrico.dose: ≥15 kg: **200 µg/kg** as adult. <15 kg / <5 y: restricted on many labels — specialist/protocol only.
pediatrico.notes: Household scabies: treat contacts + environmental measures.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Pruritus, dizziness, nausea, diarrhea; Mazzotti reaction in onchocerciasis (fever, urticaria, lymphadenopathy).
